# House rules

These rules apply to every project built on this core. They are read by Claude, GitHub Copilot and any other agent that follows AGENTS.md. The project's own `AGENTS.md` adds to these and wins where the two differ.

## How we build

1. Start from the brief in `docs/brief.md`. If it says it is not filled in yet, run the `kickoff` skill first: ask its questions one at a time and write the answers there before building anything.
2. Build every component with shadcn/ui. Use what is in `src/components/ui/`, add missing ones with `npx shadcn@latest add <name>`, and never hand-make a button, input, card or dialog. Style with Tailwind and the theme colours (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`), never hard-coded colours. Follow the `use-shadcn` skill.
3. A prototype is a rough first draft for designers to take further. Keep it simple, readable and easy to change: React, Vite, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, nothing more unless the brief asks for it.
4. The app lives in `src/`. The build publishes it, so whatever is in `src/` is what people see.
5. Record any decision worth remembering in `docs/decisions.md`, with one line on why.

## What you never do

- Never edit anything inside `.core/`. It is shared and read-only. Suggest the change instead.
- Never commit secrets, API keys, tokens or passwords. Use environment variables and say which ones are needed.
- Never use real personal data such as names, emails, phone numbers or personal identity numbers. Use clearly fake sample data.
- Never add tracking, analytics or third-party scripts without it being written in the brief.
- Never turn off or work around a check. If a check fails, fix the cause or explain why it is wrong.

## Internal tools

When `.buildkit` says `profile=internal`, the tool is for the agency itself. Type errors, vulnerable dependencies and design drift block. Its live link is public, so it uses fake data until it has private hosting.

## Client projects

When `.buildkit` says `profile=client`, these apply on top:

- Every check blocks. Never move a project to a weaker profile.
- Change `main` only through a pull request that a person reviews. Never merge or approve yourself.
- The core version is pinned. Update it on purpose with `./scripts/update-core.sh`, in its own pull request.
- Client data and credentials never go in the repo, not even as samples. Use fake data and the client's own secret store.

## Checks

Run `.core/hooks/checks/run.sh` to check the project. The same checks run in git pre-commit, after Claude edits a file, and in CI. CI is the one that counts.

## Skills

Skills live in `.core/skills/`. Use them when the task matches:

- `start-prototype` for creating a brand new prototype, from nothing to a live link
- `kickoff` for starting a new prototype and writing the brief
- `build-prototype` for building or changing a page
- `use-shadcn` for any component, layout or styling
- `ship-prototype` for publishing and sharing the live link
- `start-client` for setting up a new client project
- `ship-client` for handing over a client change as a pull request

skills.name: build-prototype
skills.description: Build or change a page in a Build Kit prototype. Use when asked to make, sketch or change anything that will be shown in the browser.
steps: Read `docs/brief.md`. If it is not filled in yet, run the `kickoff` skill first.

The app is React with Vite, Tailwind and shadcn/ui. `src/App.tsx` is the start page. Put more pages in `src/pages/<Name>.tsx` and switch between them with simple state or `#hash` links. Add a router only if the brief needs real URLs.
Build every component with shadcn/ui and style with the theme. Follow the `use-shadcn` skill.
Keep it one simple draft: fake data in a `src/data.ts` file, no backend, no login that really works.
Use fake sample content. No real names, emails or other personal data.
Preview at the localhost link the session start printed (usually http://localhost:8000). Opening the project in Claude Code starts it, or run `npm run dev`. It updates as you save.
Run `npm run typecheck` and `.core/hooks/checks/run.sh`, and fix anything that blocks.
Add a line to `docs/decisions.md` for any choice a designer would want to know about.

skills.name: kickoff
skills.description: Start a new prototype by asking the kickoff questions and writing the brief. Use when docs/brief.md is not filled in, or when someone says they want to start something new.
steps: Say in one sentence that you'll ask a few quick questions first, so the first draft is about the right thing.

Skip anything the person has already told you, for example what it is and who it's for when the project was just created. Ask the rest **one at a time**. Wait for each answer. Keep your own words short and friendly, and offer an example answer if the person seems unsure.
If an answer is vague, ask one follow-up at most, then move on. If the person answers several questions at once, or pastes a whole brief, accept it and only ask about what's missing.
When all questions are answered, write `docs/brief.md` with one short section per question, in the person's own words. Remove the line that says the brief is not filled in.
Read the brief back as three bullet points and ask if it's right.
Only then start building, using the `build-prototype` skill.
questions: Who is it for? Who will use it, and who will look at the prototype?
The moment. When does someone need this? What are they trying to get done?
What should they see or do? The two or three things the prototype must show.
The one thing it must get right. If only one thing works, what should it be?
How should it feel? Three words, or a reference you like.
Out of scope. What should it clearly not try to do yet?
Data. Does it touch any real personal or client data? If yes, we use fake sample data and note it here.
Feedback. Who gives feedback, and what kind of feedback do you want?

skills.name: ship-client
skills.description: Hand over a change in a client project as a pull request for review. Use when asked to ship, deliver, push or share work in a project whose .buildkit says profile=client.
steps: Work on a branch, never on `main`: `git switch -c <short-description>`. The pre-push hook stops pushes to `main`.
Run `.core/hooks/checks/run.sh`. In the client profile every check blocks, so all of them must pass, including `typecheck`, `dependency-audit` and `licences`.
Commit with messages that say what changed for the client, not how.

Push the branch and open a pull request with `gh pr create`. In the description, write what changed, how to look at it, and anything the reviewer should check by hand (copy, accessibility, edge cases).
Tell the person the pull request link and who should review it, as named in `docs/brief.md`.
Never merge it yourself and never approve it. A person reviews and merges.
After the merge, CI builds the site on `main` and keeps it as a download on the run. Deploying it to the client's hosting follows the plan in `docs/brief.md`.

skills.name: ship-prototype
skills.description: Publish a Build Kit prototype and share its live link. Use when asked to deploy, publish, ship or share the prototype.
steps: Run `.core/hooks/checks/run.sh`. Nothing may block.
Commit with a short message that says what changed for the person looking at it.
Push to `main`. CI runs the same checks, builds the app and publishes it to GitHub Pages.
The live link is `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`. The repo README shows it too.
Share the link together with one sentence on what to look at and what kind of feedback you want.

skills.name: start-client
skills.description: Set up a new client project from the client template. Use when someone needs a repo for real client work, a delivery or a production site, not a quick prototype.
steps: Ask one question: which client and what is the delivery? Suggest a repo name in lowercase with dashes, like `acme-booking`, and ask for a go-ahead in one message: "I'll create `acme-booking` as a private repo on your GitHub. OK?" Their yes is the approval for step 2.

Follow step 2 of the `start-prototype` skill with the template `hansalbertisaksson/template-client`, and create the repo with `--private` instead of `--public`. `go-live.sh` sees the client profile and skips the public link.
When it prints `READY`, run `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<folder> <folder>/scripts/session-start.sh`, then follow the `kickoff` skill inside `<folder>`, including the client questions.
Build with `build-prototype` and `use-shadcn`. Hand over every change with `ship-client`.

Tell the person once: in GitHub, under Settings, Branches, protect `main` so it needs a review. On a free personal account this needs a public repo or a paid plan. Until then the pre-push hook and the house rules keep `main` behind pull requests.

skills.name: start-prototype
skills.description: Start a new prototype or internal tool, from nothing to a live link. Use when someone asks to build a prototype, demo, mockup, quick site, page, app, dashboard or internal tool for a client, the agency or a pitch, and there is no Build Kit project folder for it yet. Use this instead of making a claude.ai artifact.
steps: **Check the GitHub CLI.** `gh auth status`. If `gh` is missing, ask the person if you may run `brew install gh`. If they are not logged in, ask them to type `! gh auth login` here, choose GitHub.com, HTTPS and "Login with a web browser". It happens only once.
**Check Node.** `npm --version`. If it is missing, ask if you may run `brew install node`.
**Create the repo**, unless it already exists from an earlier try:

**Copy it to the Mac** over HTTPS with the GitHub CLI's login, so it works without SSH keys. Skip this if `~/GitHub/<name>/.git` already exists. GitHub needs a few seconds to fill a new repo, so try up to five times, a few seconds apart:
**Set it up and switch on the live link:** `cd ~/GitHub/<name> && ./scripts/setup.sh && .core/scripts/go-live.sh`. It prints `READY` with the links, or a line starting with `STOPPED`.

skills.name: use-shadcn
skills.description: Build every component with shadcn/ui and style with the theme. Use whenever adding or changing a component, a layout, colours, type or spacing.
steps: Check `src/components/ui/` for the component you need. The template comes with button, card, badge, input, label, textarea, select, checkbox, switch, tabs, dialog, avatar, table, progress, separator and skeleton.
If it's missing, add it with `npx shadcn@latest add <name>` (for example `npx shadcn@latest add dropdown-menu sheet`). Look at the full list on ui.shadcn.com before building anything by hand.
Compose pages from these components. For whole sections such as a login, a dashboard or a sidebar, start from a shadcn block (`npx shadcn@latest add login-03`) and adapt it.
Import from `@/components/ui/<name>`. Icons come from `lucide-react`.

Style with Tailwind classes and the theme colours only: `bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border`, `bg-card`, `text-destructive` and the other names in `src/index.css`.
Change the look in one place: the CSS variables in `src/index.css`. Record the change in `docs/decisions.md`.

checks.description: Looks for API keys, tokens and private keys.
Looks for Swedish and Norwegian personal identity numbers.
Stops files over 5 MB from being committed. Large media belongs in a shared drive or a CDN.
Flags hard-coded colours so everything visual comes from the theme in src/index.css.
Flags hand-made buttons, inputs and dialogs so every component comes from shadcn/ui.
